evals.prompt: Prepare a local NVFLARE POC workspace under /tmp/nvflare/poc-demo, start it, and tell me when it is ready.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to nvflare-poc-workflow, treats the request as explicit prepare/start intent, runs nvflare poc prepare and nvflare poc start, verifies readiness with nvflare system status --format json and/or nvflare agent doctor --format json, and does not use nvflare poc status.
assertions: The selected skill is nvflare-poc-workflow.
The agent uses nvflare poc prepare for workspace preparation.
The agent uses nvflare poc start for explicit startup intent.
The agent verifies readiness with nvflare system status --format json and/or nvflare agent doctor --format json.
The agent does not use nvflare poc status.
The final response reports observed readiness evidence or the current blocker.

mandatory_behavior.description: runs POC prepare/start only because the user explicitly asked to prepare and start a local POC workspace
checks local POC readiness using nvflare system status --format json and/or nvflare agent doctor --format json
reports observed readiness evidence, partial readiness, or a current blocker instead of ending with a vague availability statement

prohibited_behavior.description: does not use nonexistent or unsupported nvflare poc status
does not use deprecated nvflare job create
does not inspect NVFLARE SDK source or docstrings to discover or override public CLI command guidance
does not prepare, start, stop, clean, or kill POC processes unless the user explicitly requested that operation
does not finish with a generic standing-by message without observed readiness, shutdown evidence, or a current blocker

process_metrics.description: whether the first skill selection chooses nvflare-poc-workflow for local POC operations
whether POC commands match the explicit user intent and avoid unsupported or deprecated commands
whether final output cites observed system status, doctor readiness, shutdown state, or a current blocker
number of POC mutations or process kills attempted without explicit user intent and required confirmation
number of nvflare poc status, nvflare job create, or SDK-source command-discovery attempts

evals.prompt: Check whether my local NVFLARE POC system is running and healthy. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to nvflare-poc-workflow, performs read-only verification using nvflare system status --format json and/or nvflare agent doctor --format json, and does not run mutating POC or job commands.
assertions: The selected skill is nvflare-poc-workflow.
The agent treats the request as read-only verification.
The agent uses nvflare system status --format json and/or nvflare agent doctor --format json.
The agent does not run nvflare poc prepare, nvflare poc start, nvflare poc stop, nvflare poc clean, job submit, or process kill commands.
The agent does not use nvflare poc status.

mandatory_behavior.description: uses only read-only status and doctor evidence for verify/check-local-POC-running prompts
checks readiness using nvflare system status --format json and/or nvflare agent doctor --format json

prohibited_behavior.description: does not use nonexistent or unsupported nvflare poc status
does not prepare, start, stop, clean, submit jobs, or kill processes during read-only verification
does not finish with a generic standing-by message without observed readiness or a current blocker

evals.prompt: Stop my local NVFLARE POC workspace, but do not interrupt active jobs.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to nvflare-poc-workflow, treats the request as explicit stop intent, checks active jobs with nvflare job list --format json, blocks or asks when visible active job IDs exist, and runs nvflare poc stop only when it is safe or explicitly approved.
assertions: The selected skill is nvflare-poc-workflow.
The agent uses nvflare job list --format json before stopping.
The agent detects visible active job IDs and asks or blocks instead of stopping immediately.
The agent runs nvflare poc stop only with explicit stop intent and no active-job blocker or after explicit approval.
The agent reports stopped evidence or the active-job blocker.

mandatory_behavior.description: runs nvflare poc stop only when the user explicitly asks to stop the POC
checks nvflare job list --format json before stopping and surfaces visible active job IDs
asks or blocks when active job IDs are visible and the user asked not to interrupt jobs

prohibited_behavior.description: does not stop POC unless the user explicitly requested stop
does not finish without stopped evidence, active-job IDs, or a current blocker

evals.prompt: Clean my local POC workspace at /tmp/nvflare/poc-demo. Force it if there are no active jobs.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to nvflare-poc-workflow, treats the prompt as explicit clean intent, checks active jobs first, and runs nvflare poc clean --force only after explicit force/confirmation and no active-job blocker.
assertions: The selected skill is nvflare-poc-workflow.
The agent recognizes explicit clean and force intent.
The agent uses nvflare job list --format json before cleaning.
The agent runs nvflare poc clean --force only after explicit force/confirmation and no active-job blocker.
The agent does not use broad filesystem deletion as a substitute for the POC clean command.

mandatory_behavior.description: runs POC clean only when the user explicitly asks to clean the local POC workspace
checks nvflare job list --format json before cleaning POC workspace state
uses nvflare poc clean --force only after explicit force or confirmation from the user

prohibited_behavior.description: does not clean or force-clean POC workspace state without explicit clean intent
does not replace nvflare poc clean with broad rm -rf cleanup of guessed workspace directories
does not finish without clean/shutdown evidence or a current blocker

evals.prompt: My POC start is blocked by orphaned local processes. Find the stale POC processes and recover, but ask me before killing anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to nvflare-poc-workflow, loads cleanup/recovery guidance, gathers pid/process evidence, presents candidate PID evidence, asks for explicit confirmation before killing, attempts graceful termination first, and avoids broad kill-by-name behavior.
assertions: The selected skill is nvflare-poc-workflow.
The agent treats the prompt as orphan recovery, not normal job diagnosis.
The agent gathers process evidence and presents a candidate PID table before any kill.
The agent asks for explicit confirmation before killing candidate PIDs.
The agent tries graceful termination before forceful kill.
The agent does not kill processes by broad name match alone.

mandatory_behavior.description: uses the POC cleanup/recovery guidance for orphaned local POC process recovery
collects PID, command, parent, workspace, and age evidence before recommending process termination
presents candidate PIDs and why each appears tied to the stale POC workspace
asks for explicit user confirmation before terminating candidate PIDs
attempts graceful termination before forceful kill when recovery is confirmed

prohibited_behavior.description: does not kill all matching process names without PID/workspace evidence and confirmation
does not kill or clean POC processes unless the user explicitly requested recovery
does not finish without observed recovery evidence, remaining blockers, or explicit confirmation needed

evals.prompt: My POC is already running. Submit the exported FLARE job in evals/files/exported-basic, monitor it, and download the results.
evals.expected_output: The POC workflow skill should not be the lead; already-running POC plus exported-job submit/monitor/download intent routes to nvflare-job-lifecycle.
assertions: The selected skill is nvflare-job-lifecycle, not nvflare-poc-workflow.
The agent treats the running POC as target context for job lifecycle work.
The agent does not prepare, start, stop, or clean the POC for a submit/monitor/download request.
The agent does not use deprecated nvflare job create.

mandatory_behavior.description: routes exported-job submit, monitor, and download work to nvflare-job-lifecycle once POC is already running

prohibited_behavior.description: does not use deprecated nvflare job create
does not prepare, start, stop, or clean the POC when the user asked for job lifecycle work

evals.prompt: Convert this raw PyTorch training script into an NVFLARE federated job and then I will run it locally: evals/files/raw-pytorch/train.py.
evals.expected_output: The POC workflow skill should not trigger; raw framework training code routes to nvflare-convert-pytorch.
assertions: The selected skill is nvflare-convert-pytorch, not nvflare-poc-workflow.
The agent does not run POC prepare/start just because the user eventually plans local execution.
The agent does not submit raw framework code as an exported FLARE job.

prohibited_behavior.description: does not prepare or start POC while handling raw training-code conversion

evals.prompt: My POC job job-456 failed with EXECUTION_EXCEPTION on one client. Diagnose the root cause and tell me how to fix it.
evals.expected_output: The POC workflow skill should not be the lead; root-cause failure diagnosis routes to nvflare-diagnose-job.
assertions: The selected skill is nvflare-diagnose-job, not nvflare-poc-workflow.
The agent treats failed job root-cause analysis as diagnosis, not POC lifecycle management.
The agent does not stop, clean, or restart POC unless explicitly requested as a recovery action after diagnosis.

mandatory_behavior.description: routes failed or suspicious POC job root-cause requests to nvflare-diagnose-job

prohibited_behavior.description: does not stop, clean, or restart POC just because a job failed
